newsitem.title: UK: Lehman raises year-end FTSE 100 forecast to 3,700.
newsitem.headline: Lehman raises year-end FTSE 100 forecast to 3,700.

text.p: Strategists at Lehman Brothers raised their year-end forecast for the UK's FTSE 100 index after their view on the market's prospects for this year proved too bearish, a research note from the brokerage said on Thursday.
Strategists Ian Scott and Joe Rooney said they increased their forecast for the FTSE at the end of 1996 to 3,700 from 3,350, and set a mid 1997 target of 4,050 for the blue chip UK stock index.
Yet the new 1996 year-end forecast is still below the current level of the FTSE, which on September 10 hit an all-time intraday peak of 3,933.6.

Lehman said gilt yields had so far this year been lower than it had expected, helping underpin share prices, but it expected higher yields by year-end that would put renewed pressure on the equity market.
